<challenge>
Design and build the strongest Gmail-inspired email application you can.

Recreate the clarity, information density, speed, and familiar workflows of a great modern inbox. Take the implementation as far as you can: choose the stack, scope, visual direction, data model, and technical limits that let you deliver the most convincing complete product.
</challenge>

<essential-outcomes>
The finished application must include:

- A polished, responsive mail shell with a recognizable inbox, navigation, toolbar, search, and account controls.
- A realistic seeded mailbox with varied senders, subjects, timestamps, labels, read states, attachments, threads, and message content.
- Functional mailbox navigation for at least Inbox, Starred, Sent, Drafts, and Trash.
- Working message selection, read/unread state, starring, archiving, deleting, and labeling.
- A usable search experience that filters or retrieves relevant mail.
- A message-reading view with a clear conversation hierarchy and useful actions.
- A compose experience with recipients, subject, body, draft behavior, send behavior, and a polished interaction model.
- Responsive behavior that remains coherent and usable on both desktop and mobile.
</essential-outcomes>

<product-depth>
Go beyond a static visual recreation. Interactions should update the interface consistently, preserve state where useful, and make the product feel alive. You may add keyboard shortcuts, bulk actions, category tabs, snoozing, scheduled mail, contact suggestions, rich composition, settings, themes, offline persistence, or any other details that strengthen the experience.

No external email account, authentication, paid service, or API key is required. A fully local product with excellent seeded data and convincing behavior is valid. Do not leave prominent controls as decorative placeholders when a meaningful local interaction can be implemented.
</product-depth>

<creative-freedom>
You have broad freedom over architecture, libraries, layout details, interaction design, copy, and visual polish. Use Gmail as the product reference, but make deliberate decisions and deliver a coherent application rather than a collection of disconnected screens.

Do not explain your design before building it. Make the product and engineering decisions yourself, implement the experience, test the important workflows, and refine it into the best result you can.
</creative-freedom>

<success-criteria>
The result should immediately read as a high-quality email client, reward exploration, and support a convincing end-to-end flow from finding a message to reading, organizing, composing, and sending mail. Visual fidelity matters, but functional depth, consistency, responsiveness, and product judgment matter just as much.
</success-criteria>

Work only inside the current working directory. Do not read, list, search, or edit files outside the current working directory. Treat it as a standalone project root.
During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port 9387, then use that port for runtime verification.
Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm.
Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title.
Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory.

**Architecting My Masterpiece**

The package installation is complete, allowing me to now focus on meticulously planning the architecture, data model, visual design, and interactive features. I'm thoroughly reviewing all requirements and opportunities to ensure this Gmail-inspired application is truly exceptional.

**Defining My Branding**

I've solidified the core branding elements: `Gemini 4 Argon` for both the browser tab and the main visible header. My focus has now shifted to a detailed aesthetic, aiming for a Google Material 3 Expressive Workspace look, encompassing both light and dark modes with specific color palettes for various UI components and an adjustable display density.

**Refining My Layout**

I'm now deep into the granular details of the inbox layout. I've finalized display density options, including comfortable and compact modes, and am implementing split view functionality for optimal thread exploration. I'm also ensuring zero layout shift during hover states and applying tabular numerals for consistent timestamp and counter display.

**Generating My Content**

I'm now focused on populating the application with data. Specifically, I'm creating around 28 realistic email threads across various categories and folders, complete with multi-message conversations, quoted text, and attachments. I'm also designing an interactive attachment preview modal for users to inspect or download files.

**Implementing My Navigation**

I'm now meticulously coding the left-hand navigation sidebar and its various system views. My current focus is on implementing the collapsible behavior, ensuring the prominent "Compose" button's styling is just right, and setting up the badges for unread, starred, snoozed, and draft counts.

**Developing My Functionality**

I'm now integrating advanced search capabilities, including full-text searching across multiple fields and supporting Gmail operators. I'm also implementing interactive quick filter chips and an autocomplete popover for a seamless search experience.

**Refining My Filters**

I'm now detailing the advanced search modal and its structured filtering options. This includes implementing controls for 'From', 'To', 'Subject', and text content, alongside size, date range, and attachment presence, all designed to integrate seamlessly with the existing search bar.

**Implementing My Actions**

I'm now focusing on the interaction shortcuts. I'm implementing keyboard commands for marking emails as read or unread, snoozing with a date picker, starring, and assigning labels. I'm also building out the folder move menu and refining the right-hand toolbar with navigation and split-pane controls.

**Expanding My Functionality**

I'm now refining thread display, including collapsed summaries, individual message expansion, and bulk open/close controls. The message card design incorporates sender details, timestamps, and action buttons, with interactive elements within the rich message body for things like calendar RSVPs.

**Composing My Drafts**

I'm now refining the inline and floating composer interfaces. This involves implementing sender controls, rich formatting, attachment uploads, and schedule send options. I'm also focusing on the multi-draft management within the floating window and contact token input for recipients.

**Refining My Composers**

I'm now polishing the composer experience. This includes implementing a dynamic contact autocomplete dropdown, rich text formatting with quick templates, file attachment simulation, and precise send/schedule functionality. The post-send snackbar with an undo option is also a key focus for a seamless user flow.

**Implementing My Shortcuts**

I'm now integrating comprehensive Gmail keyboard shortcuts for composition, navigation, and thread management. Additionally, I'm implementing a functional 'Undo' snackbar for restored states and a detailed help modal detailing all shortcuts and search operators.

**Structuring My Application**

I've established the foundational project structure within `src/`, defining TypeScript interfaces for all mail-related entities. My focus is now on seeding realistic data and developing the core search query parser, while also beginning to implement the main header component with its various interactive elements.

**Designing My Components**

I'm now focused on the granular implementation of key UI components. This includes refining the sidebar with live badges for folders and custom label management, building out the contextual toolbar with various bulk actions and navigation controls, and meticulously crafting the thread list and view components with detailed message cards and interactive elements.

**Generating Seed Data**

I'm focusing on populating `src/data/seedData.ts` with a comprehensive and lifelike collection of contacts, custom labels, and 28 diverse email threads spanning primary, promotions, social, and updates categories and folders. This will provide a robust foundation for testing.

content.text:
Built and verified the **Gemini 4 Argon** email client running on port `9387`.

### Key Capabilities Implemented
- **Material 3 Workspace Shell & Customization** (`src/App.tsx`, `src/components/Header.tsx`, `src/components/QuickSettingsDrawer.tsx`):
  - Full-viewport Gmail shell with collapsible navigation rail (`248px` expanded / `72px` mini rail on desktop, slide-over drawer on mobile).
  - Live **Density Switcher** (`Default` with inline attachment chips, `Comfortable`, `Compact`), **Split Reading Pane** (`No split`, `Right of inbox`, `Below inbox`), and **Light / Dark Theme** parity persisted in `localStorage`.
  - Account switcher popover with storage meter, workspace status indicator (`Active`, `Mute notifications`, `Away`), and one-click demo mailbox reset.
- **Seeded Mailbox, Folders & Custom Labels** (`src/data/seedData.ts`, `src/components/Sidebar.tsx`):
  - 24 realistic multi-message engineering, finance, product, legal, travel, social, and automated alert threads across **Inbox** (`Primary`, `Promotions`, `Social`, `Updates` category tabs), **Starred**, **Snoozed**, **Important**, **Sent**, **Scheduled**, **Drafts**, **All Mail**, **Spam**, and **Trash**.
  - Custom color-coded labels (`Engineering`, `Product`, `Finance`, `Urgent`, `Design`, `Legal`, `Travel`) with live unread/thread counters and inline label creation/deletion.
- **Triage, Bulk Actions & Search Engine** (`src/components/Toolbar.tsx`, `src/components/ThreadList.tsx`, `src/utils/searchParser.ts`):
  - Contextual action toolbar with group selection (`All`, `None`, `Read`, `Unread`, `Starred`, `Unstarred`), bulk archive, spam, delete, mark read/unread, snooze presets, move-to-folder, and label assignment.
  - Zero-layout-shift hover action rail on every thread row (`Archive`, `Delete`, `Mark read/unread`, `Snooze`).
  - Instant search parser supporting free text, structured filter chips (`Has attachment`, `Is unread`, `Starred`, `Last 7 days`), advanced search popover, and Gmail query syntax (`from:`, `to:`, `subject:`, `label:`, `category:`, `in:`, `has:attachment`, `is:unread`, `is:starred`).
- **Conversation Reader, Attachment Lightbox & Compose Dock** (`src/components/ThreadView.tsx`, `src/components/ComposeDock.tsx`, `src/components/AttachmentPreviewModal.tsx`):
  - Accordion message stack with expandable security/routing header metadata (`from`, `to`, `cc`, `date`, `TLS/DKIM`), interactive calendar invite RSVP widget (`Yes` / `Maybe` / `No`), smart-reply chips, and inline reply/reply-all/forward composer.
  - Rich floating compose dock (`Minimize`, `Maximize`, `Save & Close`) with contact autocomplete chips, `Cc`/`Bcc`, canned response templates, file attachment uploads, **Schedule Send**, and **Undo Send** snackbar notifications.
  - Full keyboard shortcut navigation (`c`, `/`, `?`, `j`/`k`, `o`/`Enter`, `u`/`Esc`, `x`, `s`, `e`, `#`).All verification checks and the production build passed with zero errors, and the **Gemini 4 Argon** mail application is live and serving on `http://localhost:9387`. No further follow-up actions are needed.
